nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the canopy and the gaps along streams drives growth in this warm, wet forest.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: The Suva side of Viti Levu is very wet, which keeps the forest green and its creeks running.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and decaying wood build the soil that the rainforest plants root in.

nodes.name: Waisila Creek
nodes.desc: Streams and pools run through the reserve and feed the creeks and rivers downstream.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria and litter animals
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit through much of the year in tropical forests and feed many birds and bats.

nodes.name: Big-leaf mahogany
nodes.desc: Planted here in the mid 1900s, it now forms much of the tall canopy beside the older native trees.

nodes.name: Tree fern
nodes.desc: A large fern of the damp forest floor and stream edges, shading the ground and sheltering small animals.

nodes.name: Breadfruit
nodes.desc: A Pacific fruit tree grown by islanders for centuries; bats are recorded eating its fruit.

nodes.name: African tulip tree
nodes.desc: An introduced, invasive tree with nectar-rich flowers that attract birds and insects.

nodes.name: Insular flying fox
nodes.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, pollen and nectar, so it both feeds on and pollinates forest trees.

nodes.name: Barking imperial pigeon
nodes.desc: A large fruit-eating pigeon that swallows big fruits, giving trees a way to spread seeds.

nodes.name: Masked shining parrot
nodes.desc: A big parrot found only on Viti Levu, living in lowland and hill forest and gardens.

nodes.name: Collared lory
nodes.desc: Eats fruit, seeds, nectar and blossoms, and favors African tulip flowers.

nodes.name: Kikau (wattled honeyeater)
nodes.desc: A lively nectar-feeding honeyeater of Fijian forest and gardens, likely a pollinator of flowers.

nodes.name: Red-vented bulbul
nodes.desc: An introduced bird, brought to Fiji in 1903, that eats fruit, nectar and insects.

nodes.name: Great eggfly (blue moon)
nodes.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on forest-edge plants; adults visit flowers.

nodes.name: Fiji tree frog
nodes.desc: A small native frog of forest floors and streams, hunting insects at night.

nodes.name: Fiji green emo skink
nodes.desc: A native skink, a small lizard of Fiji forests that eats small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Vanikoro flycatcher
nodes.desc: Mainly catches insects from a perch, and also takes lizards and small fruits.

nodes.name: Cane toad
nodes.desc: Released in Fiji in 1953; it eats a wide range of invertebrates and small vertebrates.

nodes.name: Small Indian mongoose
nodes.desc: An introduced predator that eats insects, reptiles, amphibians and ground-nesting birds.

nodes.name: Fiji goshawk
nodes.desc: Fiji's top forest raptor; it takes birds up to pigeon size, reptiles, insects and rodents.
